newsitem.title: FRANCE: French insurer UAP shows first-half profit.
newsitem.headline: French insurer UAP shows first-half profit.

text.p: France's biggest insurer, Union des Assurances de Paris, announced on Tuesday it returned to profit in the first half after racking up a large loss in 1995 and said it was on track to achieve "lasting profitability."

UAP, which launched a sweeping recovery programme at the start of 1996, said net attributable profit rose to 860 million francs ($166.3 million) from 806 million francs a year earlier on consolidated premium income that rose 6.6 percent to 86.4 billion francs.
The results marked a turnaround for UAP, Europe's second largest insurance group, which posted a full-year 1995 loss of 2.07 billion francs, the first in its history.
The loss included an exceptional second-half charge of 4.5 billion francs for provisions against doubtful property loans following the collapse of French real estate prices.
"We're on the right track," UAP chairman Jacques Friedman told reporters, adding the results were built on a "healthy basis" and came in the face of a big fall in capital gains.
Earnings were powered by a strong improvement in insurance profits which climbed 14.4 percent to 2.03 billion francs.

Shares in UAP, whose performance has sorely disappointed investors since its privatisation in 1994, rose nearly four percent but then retreated to close up just 1.40 percent at 108.50 francs. The company was sold off at 152 francs.

Insurance analysts said UAP, whose results were hammered in previous years by provisions to cover exposure to France's long-running property slump, had made big strides but still had room for improvement.
"The results are robust given their past problems...but compared to the rest of the market, they've got a long way to go," said Deutsche Bank analyst Jean-Baptiste Bellon.
Friedmann announced at the start of the year a drive to cut costs, slash debt, restructure international operations and dispose of assets to restore profitability.
"These (results) are the first effects," he said. He said doubtful property loans were now limited to just 1.1 billion francs and that risk provisioning was now 69 percent.
"For the first time in several years, the improvement in our operational result is finally showing through in our net consolidated profit," he said.
He forecast UAP would generate a second half profit similar to that of the first half and said he expected a "significant" rise for 1997.

Friedmann sought to bury takeover rumours which have stalked UAP since the start of the year, saying he did not know of any company interested in taking over UAP. Most recently, Axa denied it was interested in UAP.
Profits from banking activities soared to 245 million francs from 61 million francs, helped by a strong performance by French bank BNP in which it holds a 15 percent stake.
Its troubled Banque Worms unit, whose property woes were in the past a huge drag on profits, cut its losses to 26 million francs from a loss of 63 million.
But the loss from holding companies deepened to 776 million francs from a loss of 422 million, reflecting exceptional charges of 535 million for losses on disposals.
Debt was expected to fall to eight billion francs at the end of 1996 from 10 billion francs at the end of June. ($1=5.172 French Franc)
